chunks: And Isma'il ibn Jabir narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:
I said to him: Tell me about the prayer of the two Eids—are there an adhan and an iqamah in them?

He said: There is neither adhan nor iqamah in them, but it is called out, 'al-salat, al-salat,' three times. There is no minbar in them; the minbar is not moved from its place. Rather, something resembling a minbar is made of clay for the Imam, so he stands upon it and addresses the people, then he comes down.

key_terms.إِقَامَةٌ: the second call announcing the immediate start of salat
key_terms.الصَّلَاةَ: the proclamation calling people to the prayer
key_terms.صَلَاةَ الْعِيدَيْنِ: the prayer of the two Eids, meaning Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha
key_terms.طِينٍ: clay, used here for making a temporary raised structure
key_terms.فَيَخْطُبُ: then he delivers a sermon to the people
key_terms.مِنْبَرٌ: the pulpit from which the Imam gives the sermon

ai.seo_question: Is there an adhan or iqamah for Eid prayer in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the legal form of the prayer of the two Eids in Shia fiqh. It states that there is no adhan or iqamah for Eid prayer; instead, the call 'al-salat' is announced three times, and the Imam delivers the sermon from a temporary clay structure rather than moving the established minbar.
